title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 729–731): S is a connected scheme over Q with geometric point s̄. A is an abelian group with a homomorphism j : A → G_m(S) = H^0(S, O_S^*). T = Ẑ(1) = lim μ_n is the Tate module of G_m. Kummer theory gives an action of π_1(S, s̄) on the torsor of compatible n-th roots of the units j(a). This yields γ_j : π_1 → G_j = Hom(A, T) ⋊ Ẑ^*, lying over the cyclotomic character χ : π_1 → Ẑ^*. Put π_1^+ = Ker χ. Restricting gives γ_j^+ : π_1^+ → Hom(A, T), the Kummer pairing over the cyclotomic tower. With Π̃_1 = Im γ_j, Π̃_1^+ = Im γ_j^+ and Γ = Im χ there is an exact sequence 1 → Π̃_1^+ → Π̃_1 → Γ → 1.

On this page Grothendieck wants to estimate the 'size' of Π̃_1^+ ⊂ Hom(A, T). He notes in the margin that Hom(A, T) ≃ Hom(A, Ẑ) only non-canonically. He assumes (355):
1) A is a finitely generated Z-module;
2) S is essentially of finite type over Q and normal;
3) j : A → G_m(S) is injective.

Reductions:
- Hypothesis 2 already gives Γ open in Ẑ^*, because the field of constants of the function field is a number field.
- Normality (with connectedness) makes Gal(K̄/K) → π_1(S) surjective, K being the function field. So Π̃_1^+ and Γ are unchanged on replacing S by its generic point, and one may assume S = Spec K with K finitely generated over Q.
- Conversely, one may shrink S to be affine and smooth over Q.
- He then introduces the dual Ǎ = Hom_Z(A, Z), so that Hom(A, T) ≅ Ǎ ⊗ T = Ǎ(1) (next page).

The aim, stated on the next page, is to show Π̃_1^+ is open in Ǎ(1). This is the classical open-image theorem of Kummer theory for G_m over finitely generated fields. He also asks whether surjectivity holds when A is the full unit group of a normal Z-model, or when G_m(S)/A is torsion-free.
errors: No error on this page itself; the reductions to the generic point and to an affine smooth model are correct for S normal and connected.

Context (next page): the speculation that π_1^+ → Hom(A, T) should be surjective when G_m(S)/A is torsion-free, or when A is the full unit group, fails at the prime 2. Take S_1 = Spec Z[1/2], A = {±1} × 2^Z. Then √2 ∈ Q(μ_8), so the image of π_1^+ = Gal(Q̄/Q(μ_∞)) in the 2-component has index ≥ 2. Openness is the correct statement; surjectivity is not.

ideas.what: Kummer representation of π_1(S) on roots of units, split into a cyclotomic part Γ ⊂ Ẑ^* and a 'geometric/Kummer' part Π̃_1^+ ⊂ Hom(A, Ẑ(1))
ideas.modern_name: Kummer theory / Kummer torsor of a unit; 1-motive [A → G_m] Galois representation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Kummer); open image for finitely generated subgroups of K^*: Bashmakov, Schinzel, Ribet (1979, 'Kummer theory on extensions of abelian varieties by tori')
ideas.where_published: Possibly sketched in La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981)

ideas.what: Openness of the cyclotomic character image for fields finitely generated over Q
Reduction from a normal scheme of finite type to its generic point, using surjectivity of Gal(K) → π_1(S)
ideas.modern_name: SGA1 V 8.2 surjectivity for normal schemes

deep.surprise_reason: This is the routine setup of Kummer-theoretic open image for units over finitely generated fields, a well-known result (Bashmakov/Ribet). The only mild interest is the next page's surjectivity speculation, which is false at 2.
transcription_corrections: 'j: A → Pic(S)' should be 'j: A → G_m(S)' (consistent with (350)).
'⊂ Hom(A, Ẑ)' in line 1 should be '⊂ Hom(A, T)'; the marginal note reads '≃ Hom(A, Ẑ) non canonique!'.
'dans le cas où S anabélien[?]' is more likely 'dans le cas où on suppose'.
'S absolument de type fini' should be 'S ess.t (essentiellement) de type fini sur Q et normal'.
'les groupes étendus' is likely 'les groupes envisagés'.
'Notons enfin, posons' is likely 'Notons aussi, posant'.
